extracted.intended_audience: students of philosophy, educators and lawmakers interested in designing an ideal civic education and selecting rulers
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive program for educating and selecting guardian-philosophers: curricular sequence (mathematical sciences → dialectic), character and aptitude criteria for candidates, pedagogic methods, age milestones and stages of training leading to rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic as essential study
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic must be prescribed and pursued until one 'sees the nature of numbers with the mind only' — not as merchants or for buying and selling, but for military use and the improvement of the soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be pursued 'in the spirit of a philosopher, and not of a shopkeeper.' Arithmetic compels the soul to reason about abstract number and to repel incorporation of visible/tangible objects into argument; even dull minds trained in arithmetic become quicker. Anti-pattern: studying arithmetic only for commerce or practical calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry oriented to eternal being
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometry taught must aim at knowledge of the eternal (being) rather than transient becoming; it should 'compel us to view being' rather than address only practical applications like squaring and measuring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the part of geometry that draws the soul toward truth; avoid confining instruction to narrow practical operations. Geometry's higher part is necessary for philosophical vision and military applications only in small measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomy as rational, not merely observational
rubrics_metrics.description: Astronomy is valuable when it 'compels the soul to look upwards' toward higher knowledge, but the true motions and absolute relations are apprehended by reason, not by sight of the heavens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the visible heavens as a pattern for higher truths; avoid wasting effort on exact empirical measurements of visible phenomena. The astronomer should seek problems that lead beyond sensible particulars to rational principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony/music studied for natural harmonies
rubrics_metrics.description: The science of harmony should aim at the natural harmonies of number and their relation to the beautiful and good, not merely the audible intervals and 'condensed notes' as measured by ear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid teachers who focus only on heard intervals and mechanical measurement; pursue harmony insofar as it 'elevates' and connects with philosophy. If pursued for other ends, it is useless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interconnection of mathematical sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical sciences (arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, harmony) must reach a point of inter-communion and mutual affinity before they confer value for the philosophical aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They serve as handmaids to dialectic; isolated, practical, or fragmentary study of these subjects yields little real benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialectic as the highest study
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialectic is the 'coping-stone of the sciences' and the only method that goes directly to first principles, does away with hypotheses, and enables apprehension of the absolute Good and true being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialectic must be pursued after preparation in the mathematical sciences; it lifts the 'eye of the soul' and is the test of true intelligence. Anti-pattern: treating dialectic as mere eristic (contradiction for amusement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and sequence of studies
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a particular sequence: start with plane geometry, then solids in themselves (3D), then astronomy (motion of solids); mathematical elements should be presented in childhood and later unified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reverse the natural order (e.g., skipping solids in favour of revolutions). Later studies build on earlier ones; early confusion of order impedes true comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early education as pleasant, not compulsory
rubrics_metrics.description: Present calculation, geometry and other elementary instruction to children in childhood as a sort of amusement rather than under compulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freemen should not be slaves to knowledge acquisition; compulsion in bodily exercise is harmless but forced learning obtains no hold on the mind. Use enjoyable exposure (analogous to showing young horses battle) to find natural bent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character traits and natural gifts for selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates for the highest studies and eventual rule must possess natural gifts: keenness, quick powers of acquisition, good memory, love of labour, steadfastness, and ability to endure intellectual toil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mind more than the body faints from study; choose those who display unwearied solidity and relish for labour. Anti-patterns: those half-industrious or who prefer bodily exercises to learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral virtue criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected rulers must be sound in virtues such as truthfulness (hating voluntary falsehood), temperance, courage, magnificence, and generally not 'bastard' or defective in parts of virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish true sons of philosophy from 'bastards' by observing their moral consistency; defects in any virtue risk making rulers unfit and produce ridicule or harm to the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding the 'eristic' temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent students from becoming mere eristic disputants who contradict for amusement and thereby develop lawlessness and sceptical disorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay or regulate introduction of dialectic to avoid youthful love of refutation; ensure disciples are orderly and steadfast; maturity tempers eristic tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing by dialectic (ability to abandon senses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be proven by dialectic to be able to 'give up the use of sight and the other senses' and, in company with truth, attain apprehension of absolute being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dialectical trials to identify who can abstract and define ideas rationally and withstand all objections; this is a crucial selection mechanism requiring great caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training timeline and career stages
rubrics_metrics.description: A staged program: childhood elementary instruction; gymnastics and bodily training until selection (implied ~20); promotion to higher study; by thirty chosen for higher honour and dialectic testing; a proposed period (example given: five years) of philosophy study replacing gymnastics; followed by fifteen years serving in offices to gain life experience; at fifty those who have distinguished themselves ascend to contemplative study and rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific durations are normative (e.g., say five years of concentrated philosophy study, fifteen years of practical service, culminating in rule at around fifty). The stages test steadiness under temptation and real-world experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communal lifestyle for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians/ governors should have no private ordinary possessions: wives and children, maintenance and many pursuits are to be common; they receive maintenance instead of pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This communal arrangement is intended to prevent private interest from corrupting guardians' devotion to the State; guardians live as a select, shared household and focus on duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: State patronage necessary for advanced studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Difficult and neglected branches (e.g., solid geometry) require government patronage and an environment in which the State acts as director to attract disciples and produce continuous search and discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without state support, students and teachers will not pursue these arduous studies or find directors; public honour and institutional backing incentivize deep inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity of women where nature permits
rubrics_metrics.description: Women should share in the education and functions of the guardians 'as far as their natures can go'; the prescriptions for education and rule apply to women as well as men where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume the program is for men only; include capable women in the same training pathways and offices when their nature allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding premature elevation of philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is danger in introducing dialectic too early: young students taste the delight and become contradictors (puppy-dogs), undermining philosophy's reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise caution in timing dialectic instruction; ensure maturity and proper selection to prevent 'lawlessness' and social distrust of philosophy.
